newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sega to tap into booming digital camera market.
newsitem.headline: Sega to tap into booming digital camera market.

text.p: Sega Enterprises Ltd said on Wednesday it will begin selling low-priced digital cameras in Japan in a bid to tap into the booming market and lure more people to video game centres.
Its camera, called the Digio and priced at 29,800 yen ($270), will be the cheapest digital camera sold in Japan, said a spokesman for the major maker of video game players.
It will go on sale in Japan at the end of November, he said, and the company hopes to sell 150,000 of the cameras by the end of next March.
Analysts said Sega's digital camera should be very competitive with those already on the market.
Casio Computer Co Ltd introduced the first personal-use digital camera in Japan, priced at 49,800 yen ($452), in March last year. Eastman Kodak Co sells its camera for 39,800 yen ($361).

"There are good prospects of growth for low-end digital cameras, as young consumers are likely to be attracted to such image-processing gadgets," said Noboru Machida, an analyst at Nikko Research Center.
He said the domestic market for digital cameras was expected to grow to one million units in 1996, compared with 200,000 in last year.
Machida, however, also said Sega is at a slight marketing disadvantage because it does not have distribution routes to camera shops.
"Sega will likely sell most of its digital cameras through computer stores and mass retailers," he said.
Sega also hopes to use the cameras to draw people into using its game machines and to computer game centres, a spokeswoman said.
"We are examining the possibility of providing such services to our digital camera holders as setting up machines at game centres that print out images captured on the camera," she said.
Quick photo machines have become a hit in Japanese game centres and are especially popular among teenage girls.
